answer: Web-of-trust vouching resists sybils: an identity gains weight only when established peers stake their OWN standing to vouch for it, and those vouches must come from distinct, unrelated accounts — not an echo among clones. A fake on the basalt ledge has no genuine sponsors, so it stays isolated with no inbound trust. A swarm can vouch for itself endlessly, but the counting rule discounts inward-only loops, leaving the clones weightless.
